coverage_limits: OpenAlex refused further requests after 18 of 20 planned query blocks because the shared free daily budget for this network was used up, so the idea-evaluation block and the AI-versus-human-generated block were covered only by Crossref and web searches. Crossref has no abstracts for Elsevier and AOM items, so items created after 2026-04-15 were screened mostly by title; several AoM 2026 proceedings items with relevant titles but no retrievable abstract were not reported (for example Working Faster, Engaging Less; Beyond Static Profiles; Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Before and After ChatGPT; Who Contributes More to Innovation: AI or Colleagues?). AOM, SSRN and some INFORMS pages returned 403, so sample sizes come from abstracts and are often missing. AIS conference proceedings were reached through OpenAlex and targeted AISeL searches, not by browsing every track. By design I left out employee surveys relating GenAI use to self- or supervisor-rated creativity (dozens in EJIM, JKM, IR, IJIM, Technovation and AoM Proceedings), qualitative and conceptual pieces, perception or disclosure studies of AI-made work, model-only idea benchmarks, and studies of non-generative tools (for example Jia et al. 2023 AMJ and Lazar et al. 2025 AMJ on search algorithms).

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Systems: the Influence on Human Entrepreneurial Creativity
candidates.task: new venture idea generation
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 90 participants who generated new venture ideas with or without an AI system; AI use raised the number of creative, novel and useful ideas but lowered average idea novelty. The abstract does not name the AI tool, so whether it is generative AI needs checking.

candidates.title: AI-Augmented Creativity: Overcoming the Productivity Loss in Brainstorming Groups
candidates.task: group brainstorming with GPT-3
candidates.evidence: One-factor between-subjects lab experiment comparing nominal groups, interactive groups, hybrid human plus GPT-3 groups and AI-only groups; hybrid groups produced more ideas with similar brainstorming creativity. Random assignment and N are not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Team Creativity: A Dual Stage Perspective
candidates.task: team idea generation and evaluation (MBA students)
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 91 MBA students manipulating generative-AI use at the idea-generation stage, at the evaluation stage, or not at all; AI at generation raised technical goodness and usefulness of team ideas, while novelty became polarized.

candidates.title: How Do Human Creators Compete with Artificial Intelligence? An Empirical Analysis
candidates.task: artists in an online art community after generative AI tools
candidates.evidence: Difference-in-differences across genres in an online art community after generative AI tools arrived; human output volume fell and affected creators shifted toward niche and original content. Context study of real creative output.

candidates.title: Not All Doom and Gloom: ChatGPT, Knowledge Diversity, and Style Similarity in Online Communities
candidates.task: Stack Overflow posts after ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Studies Stack Overflow after the release of ChatGPT, measuring knowledge coverage with an entropy measure and community cohesion with linguistic style matching (style similarity among posts).

candidates.title: Timing Matters: How Generative AI Impacts Creativity Through Motivation and Cognitive Processes
candidates.task: idea generation with early versus late generative-AI use
candidates.evidence: Two experiments varying when generative AI is used in the creative process; early use raised the novelty of ideas through creative self-efficacy and divergent thinking, late use raised feasibility.

candidates.title: From Diversity to Novelty: How Information Elaboration Unlocks the Creative Power of AI in Teams
candidates.task: team ideation for new product development
candidates.evidence: Five preregistered randomized controlled field experiments (528 individuals in 176 teams) on generative-AI use in NPD ideation; AI raised idea diversity, variety and depth but not fluency or usefulness, and diversity became novelty only when teams elaborated information.

candidates.title: Creative Spark or Digital Dud? Generative AI’s Impact on Outcomes & Satisfaction When Brainstorming
candidates.task: brainstorming startup ideas in an entrepreneurship course
candidates.evidence: Compares a course section encouraged to use generative AI for brainstorming startup ideas (n=53) with a section brainstorming without AI (n=46); rubric scores were similar, AI users overestimated the AI benefit and were less satisfied.

candidates.title: ErnieBot Meets ChatGPT: A Cross-Cultural Examination of AI Biases and Human-AI Creative Collaboration
candidates.task: idea generation with culturally aligned versus misaligned LLMs
candidates.evidence: Study 2 compares people collaborating with an LLM from their own culture versus another culture (ChatGPT, ErnieBot); same-culture pairs on local tasks produced more useful but not more novel ideas; Study 3 uses field data.

candidates.title: A Multi-level Study of the Impact of Human-AI Interaction and Team Dynamics on Idea Generation
candidates.task: teams in an advertisement video-making competition
candidates.evidence: Field data on 257 individuals in 80 teams in an ad video competition; individual generative-AI interaction is associated with more ideas and higher idea novelty, moderated by team-level AI characteristics.

candidates.title: Recombinant Narrowness: How Generative AI Reshapes Collective Problem-Solving Dynamics
candidates.venue: Academy of Management Proceedings, vol. 2025 (abstract marked withdrawn)
candidates.task: software developer Q&A community
candidates.evidence: Synthetic difference-in-differences on more than 400,000 questions and answers by more than 135,000 developers, measuring problem complexity, solution novelty and solvers' knowledge diversity after generative AI. The AOM record is marked withdrawn; a search snippet points to a related EURAM 2025 paper, Novel solutions, narrow knowledge, which I could not verify.

candidates.title: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI’s Impact on Creative Tasks
candidates.task: flash fiction writing and song composition
candidates.evidence: Two randomized controlled experiments (flash fiction, song composition) on how generative-AI assistance interacts with general versus domain-specific human capital in creative output; AI raises the value of general cognitive ability and lowers the value of domain expertise.

candidates.title: AI Usage Enhances Creative Performance but Leads to Biased Estimates of One’s and Others Creativity
candidates.task: three sequential creativity tasks
candidates.evidence: Experiment with three sequential creativity tasks: AI use raised creative performance but led participants to underestimate their own and others' creativity, and the bias in judging others persisted after AI use stopped.

candidates.title: Employee Disclosing Artificial Intelligence Usage at Work: Unlocking the Potential for Creativity
candidates.task: employee creativity after disclosing AI use
candidates.evidence: An experiment and a multi-wave, multi-source survey test whether disclosing one's AI use raises employee creativity. Disclosure, not AI access, is manipulated, so fit with the atlas is uncertain; included for recall.

candidates.title: AI and Prior Sector Knowledge: Effects on Opportunity Recognition, Assessment, and Exploitation
candidates.task: entrepreneurial opportunity recognition
candidates.evidence: Controlled lab experiments with entrepreneurs varying the level of AI use and prior sector knowledge; AI improved opportunity assessment and exploitation but constrained creativity and novelty in opportunity recognition. The abstract does not name the AI tool.

candidates.title: The Hidden Costs of GenAI in Idea Generation: Effects on Psychological Ownership & Idea Championing
candidates.task: creative product design task
candidates.evidence: Lab experiment: 58 participants randomly assigned to a creative product design task with or without ChatGPT, then asked to champion their idea; outcomes are psychological ownership and idea championing, and the abstract does not say whether idea creativity was rated.

candidates.title: How Generative AI Reshapes Creative Work Across Innovation Processes
candidates.task: design-thinking innovation projects at an aerospace multinational
candidates.evidence: Longitudinal mixed-methods study of 38 middle managers; GenAI supported fluency, flexibility and elaboration, while its perceived contribution to originality declined in later project stages. No comparison group.

candidates.title: When and From Whom: How AI- vs Colleague-Generated Examples and Their Timing Shape Creative Ideation
candidates.task: scenario-based idea generation after seeing example ideas
candidates.evidence: 2 (AI vs human source of example ideas) x 2 (early vs late exposure) between-subjects online experiment with 233 participants; AI examples raised idea novelty, colleague examples raised feasibility, and early AI exposure strengthened novelty.

candidates.title: Leveraging Generative AI for Good: Experimental Evidence on CSR Initiative Design and Evaluation
candidates.task: designing CSR initiatives
candidates.evidence: Experiment comparing human-only, human-AI collaboration and AI-only design of CSR initiatives; AI-augmented modes had higher overall quality, AI-only designs were most novel and human-only designs most feasible.

candidates.title: First Impressions Last: Exploring When and Why AI-Human Collaboration Sequence Enhances Creativity
candidates.task: idea generation with AI-first versus human-first sequence
candidates.evidence: Two simulation-based experiments and a field experiment varying whether the AI or the person generates ideas first; in AI-first sequences, trust in AI increased anchoring on AI suggestions and reduced idea diversity and creativity.

candidates.title: The Penalty of AI-assisted Disclosure: Language Convergence, Innovation, and Market Reaction
candidates.task: corporate earnings call transcripts
candidates.evidence: Triple-difference design on quarterly earnings calls (scripted presentations vs spontaneous Q&A); language convergence measured by BERTScore increases with AI use; market reactions are also studied.

candidates.title: Assimilating generative AI into ideation work: seeding, search and human contribution
candidates.task: idea generation by professionals
candidates.evidence: Tests four configurations with 400 professionals: human-only ideation, unstructured human-GenAI collaboration, GenAI seeding, and transformational-creativity (TC) GenAI seeding; expert ratings show TC seeding raised novelty while the other AI conditions gave no reliable gains. The AOM 2026 abstract (Augmented (or Not)), apparently the same study, reports n=350 and semantic-similarity analyses.

candidates.title: Augmented Learning for Joint Creativity in Human-GenAI Co-Creation
candidates.task: repeated co-creation rounds with Midjourney and ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods studies of human-GenAI co-creation over repeated rounds (image generation with Midjourney, problem solving with ChatGPT); joint creativity did not improve over rounds and fell for less creative people, and a further study shows that guidance on idea co-development raises joint creativity.

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Roles of Generative AI in the Creative Process: Experiments on Design Work
candidates.task: design work at ideation and execution stages
candidates.evidence: Controlled lab experiments with students and field tests with professional designers; GenAI raised creativity at the brainstorming stage for all users, while at the execution stage experts spent more time without creativity gains and novices still benefited.

candidates.title: Unraveling Generative AI from a Human Intelligence Perspective: A Battery of Experiments
candidates.task: battery of human intelligence tests including creative intelligence
candidates.evidence: Online experiments benchmark GPT-4 against human participants on cognitive, emotional, creative and social intelligence tests; GPT-4 outperforms humans on creative intelligence. Context only: no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: Human–AI synergy: finding cognitive balance in idea generation for product innovation
candidates.task: idea generation for product innovation
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 123 product innovators in three conditions (no AI, moderate AI assistance, high AI assistance); moderate assistance gave the most original and feasible ideas and high assistance reduced originality (inverted U).

candidates.title: Creativity in advertising: the roles of implicit theory and AI
candidates.task: advertising creative tasks by advertising agents
candidates.evidence: Two sequential behavioral experiments on generative-AI support for advertising practitioners; incremental theorists gained fluency and flexibility with AI, with no gain in originality; a further study measures viewers' attitudes to AI-assisted work.

candidates.title: AI as a cognitive collaborator: Assimilation and accommodation in human–machine teaming for innovation
candidates.task: open-ended innovation challenge (individuals and teams)
candidates.evidence: Randomized 2 x 2 factorial field experiment with 371 professionals in South Korea (individuals vs teams, with vs without GenAI) on an open-ended innovation challenge; expert-evaluated innovation quality rose with GenAI, especially when users adopted accommodative strategies.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment
candidates.task: workplace creativity at a technology consulting firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment in which 250 employees of a Chinese technology consulting firm were randomly assigned to ChatGPT access or no access (August 2023); LLM access raised supervisor-rated creativity and external-rater novelty of employees' written ideas, especially for employees with strong metacognitive strategies.

candidates.title: The power of generative marketing: Can generative AI create superhuman visual marketing content?
candidates.venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing, 42
candidates.task: marketing images and ad creatives
candidates.evidence: Compares images from seven text-to-image models with human-made marketing images (254,400 human evaluations of quality, realism and aesthetics); with identical creative briefs, the best AI images also beat commissioned freelancers on ad creativity, and a field test compares click-through rates.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Strategic Decision-Making: Evidence from Entrepreneurs and Investors
candidates.task: generating and evaluating business strategies
candidates.evidence: Evidence from an accelerator program and a startup competition that LLMs generate and evaluate strategies at a level comparable to entrepreneurs and investors. Context only; the outcome is strategy quality rather than a creativity score.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on creativity and diversity: An empirical study of large language model-generated product ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students priced under 50 dollars
candidates.evidence: LLM-generated product ideas have higher average quality (purchase intent) than human ideas and are far more often in the top 10 percent, but are less novel per idea and less diverse as a set; a reanalysis of prior LLM creativity studies finds lower diversity throughout. Appears to be the journal version of the Wharton idea-generation working papers already collected (Girotra et al. 2023; Meincke et al. 2024).

candidates.title: AI in science: When and where it makes a difference
candidates.task: scientific publications across 170+ fields, 2005-2023
candidates.evidence: Over 80 million publications: AI use is associated with more novel and more cited research, and the effects are stronger after transformers and large language models. AI is defined broadly, not only generative AI.

candidates.title: Does AI catalyze novelty? Generative AI, resource allocation novelty, and innovation quality of high-performing manufacturing enterprises in emerging markets
candidates.task: firm-level innovation in manufacturing enterprises
candidates.evidence: Firm-level study linking generative AI to resource allocation novelty and innovation quality. No abstract was available in the API records, so the design and measures are inferred from the title only.

candidates.title: Switching Perspectives: Enhancing Generative Artificial Intelligence's Creativity, by Humans, With Design
candidates.task: egg task (design fixation)
candidates.evidence: After interviews with design-theory experts, an experiment on the egg task shows that using GenAI tools yields more ideas, does not prevent fixation, but supports idea exploration (second-order defixation). Conditions and N are not given in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Ideation Process
candidates.task: review of AI in opportunity identification, idea generation and idea screening
candidates.evidence: Narrative review (not a systematic review or meta-analysis) of AI in ideation, covering opportunity identification, idea generation, and idea screening and selection. Included for recall.

candidates.title: Human-AI Collaboration for Brainstorming: Effect of the Presence of AI Ideas on Breadth of Exploration
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-57, 2024)
candidates.task: individual brainstorming with access to GPT-3.5 ideas
candidates.evidence: Experiment (n=52) with human-only versus human+AI brainstorming, where the AI condition saw GPT-3.5-generated ideas; flexibility (breadth of exploration) was significantly higher with AI ideas. May share data with the collected Memmert et al. (2025) B&ISE paper.

candidates.title: Fostering Innovation with Generative AI: A Study on Human-AI Collaborative Ideation and User Anonymity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-58, 2025)
candidates.task: collaborative group ideation on complex problems
candidates.evidence: Randomized experiment: groups solved complex problems with or without an AI collaborator that suggested ideas (plus an LLM idea editor for anonymity); the AI's own ideas were more innovative, but it did not significantly change participants' innovativeness.

candidates.title: A Collaborative Creative Process in the Age of AI: A Comparative Analysis of Machine and Human Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-58, 2025)
candidates.task: systematic literature analysis of machine versus human creativity
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature analysis of 52 studies on how machine and human creativity differ; concludes machine creativity is novel and original but lacks intentionality and authenticity. Conceptual synthesis rather than a meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Platform Content Convergence? Investigating ChatGPT’s Impact on Airbnb Listings
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-58, 2025)
candidates.task: Airbnb listing texts before and after ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Compares Airbnb listing texts before and after the release of ChatGPT with control and treatment groups; finds a significant change in average pairwise textual similarity (content convergence).

candidates.title: Idea Generation With a Majority of AI Teammates: Exploring Productivity Effects, Process Gains and Process Losses
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 59th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-59, 2026)
candidates.task: team idea generation with AI teammates
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study with experimental methods: 66 participants in teams of three humans and four LLM teammates on an idea generation task; half of the top ideas came from AI. No no-AI comparison is described in the abstract.

candidates.title: The Confidence Cage: How Creative Self-Efficacy Hinders Gen AI-Augmented Ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 59th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-59, 2026)
candidates.task: idea generation with and without AI support (pre/post test)
candidates.evidence: Pre- and post-test experiment (N=300): AI support raised creativity through improved ideation, with larger gains for people low in creative self-efficacy.

candidates.title: Towards Generative Monoculture? Insights from a Field Experiment on Style and Content Homogenisation Effects in GenAI-Supported Knowledge Work
candidates.venue: ACIS 2025 Proceedings (Australasian Conference on Information Systems), paper 290
candidates.task: knowledge work tasks at a multinational industrial firm
candidates.evidence: Field experiment with 99 knowledge workers: outputs made with GenAI support were more homogeneous in style and content than outputs made without it, across knowledge acquisition, packaging and creation tasks; advanced prompting and critical handling may reduce the effect. OpenAlex files this paper under JAIS by mistake.

candidates.title: Fostering Divergent Thinking via Generative AI: The Role of Questioning-Based Learning
candidates.venue: ICIS 2025 Proceedings (International Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: student ideation (divergent thinking)
candidates.evidence: Field experiment with students: questioning-enhanced GenAI raised computed fluency, flexibility and originality of ideas, with adverse effects under high task difficulty; the comparison condition is not clear from the abstract.

candidates.title: AI-Enabled Fuzzy Front End: How and Why Generative AI Enhances Creativity in Raw Idea Generation
candidates.venue: ICIS 2025 Proceedings (International Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: toy design by combining two concepts
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered experiment: participants designed toys by combining two concepts with or without generative-AI assistance; AI raised rated creativity, more so for atypical (appropriateness) and abstract (novelty) combinations.

candidates.title: When AI Joins the Brainstorm: Impacts of Generative Language Models on Collaborative Divergent Thinking
candidates.venue: ICIS 2025 Proceedings (International Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: collaborative brainstorming with an AI peer
candidates.evidence: Randomized controlled experiment (N=96, four conditions) crossing the idea-sharing structure with the presence of a generative-language-model peer; AI peers produced more original ideas, but exposure to them lowered participants' fluency and originality.

candidates.title: When AI Sparks Less: Generative AI and The Decline Of Self-Perceived Creativity
candidates.venue: ECIS 2026 Proceedings (European Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: creative task with or without GenAI
candidates.evidence: Experiment with 82 participants: GenAI use lowered intrinsic task motivation and domain-relevant and creativity-relevant skills, while self-evaluated creative performance did not change. Outcomes appear mostly self-reported.

candidates.title: Balancing Efficiency and Diversity: How AI-Generated Review Summaries Reshape Tourist Reviews
candidates.venue: PACIS 2026 Proceedings (Pacific Asia Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: tourist reviews on Ctrip
candidates.evidence: Difference-in-differences around the introduction of AI-generated review summaries on Ctrip: later reviews became longer and more semantically similar to each other (homogenization), aligning with the summaries and losing within-review diversity.

candidates.title: The Janus-Faced Effects of Ideation with Generative AI on Individual Creativity and Dignity
candidates.venue: ICIS 2024 Proceedings (International Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: ideation with a custom GenAI tool (Idea Hub)
candidates.evidence: 2 x 2 between-subjects experiment varying the breadth and depth of exploration in a GenAI ideation tool; studies AI-enabled serendipity, idea enhancement and fixation on AI output as drivers of creativity performance and dignity. N not stated on the landing page.

candidates.title: Generative AI in Idea Development: The Role of Numeric and Visual Feedback
candidates.venue: ICIS 2023 Proceedings (International Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: idea development with generative-AI feedback
candidates.evidence: Experimental series in which people develop ideas with generative AI that gives numeric or visual feedback at different times, testing which co-creative arrangements help idea development. Related to but distinct from the collected Gordetzki et al. (2026) ISR paper; N not stated on the landing page.

candidates.title: The Art of Inspiring Creativity: Exploring the Unique Impact of AI-generated Images
candidates.venue: AMCIS 2023 Proceedings (Americas Conference on Information Systems)
candidates.task: idea generation after viewing DALL-E 2 images
candidates.evidence: Online experiment with 298 participants in three groups (AI-generated art from DALL-E 2, traditional art, no art); outcomes are originality and number of ideas, and AI-generated art most enhanced idea generation.

candidates.title: The rise of AI-enabled new product ideation: End of innovation crowdsourcing?
candidates.task: crowdsourced new product ideas versus AI-generated product features
candidates.evidence: Introduces AI-conceivability to compare AI-generated product features with ideas from innovation crowdsourcing and their market value. Design details come from the AMCIS 2024 landing page; the journal abstract was not available.

candidates.title: Comparing the Ideation Quality of Humans With Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.task: product and service innovation ideas
candidates.evidence: Executives blindly rated innovation ideas from human professionals and from generative AI; AI ideas scored higher on novelty and customer benefit with similar feasibility. A 2026 record with the same title appears in the same journal (54(3), 29-40).

candidates.title: Chat-GPT4 Does Enhance Creativity. But Human Ego Can Hamper its Potential
candidates.task: advertising slogan writing
candidates.evidence: Two pre-registered studies: ChatGPT-4 slogans were rated more novel, meaningful and persuasive but less diverse than human slogans; GenAI assistance raised slogan quality for less creative people but not for egocentric creators. Abstract taken from the PsyArXiv version (single author, Gill).

candidates.title: Does Generative AI Make Startup Ideas Alike? Evidence from Product Hunt
candidates.task: startup product launches on Product Hunt
candidates.evidence: 291,314 Product Hunt launches (January 2018 to April 2026): after ChatGPT, launches concentrate around common category concepts and the share of distinctive launches falls from 25 to 16 percent, more so in categories where LLMs can better assist product ideation.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Ideation and the performance of Innovation Teams (Preprint)
candidates.task: innovation team ideation with an AI-augmented tool
candidates.evidence: Framed field experiment with experimental (AI-augmented ideation tool) and control groups of innovation teams; AI teams produced higher-quality ideas in less time and showed greater idea diversity.

candidates.title: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays
candidates.task: student essays: human-only, AI-only and human+AI prompt strategies
candidates.evidence: Analyzes 6,875 essays across five conditions; AI-augmented essays gain quality but lose structural variance on some dimensions (homogenization), and specific prompts can reverse this on argument depth. How essays were assigned to conditions is not clear from the abstract. Outside the core lane journals; reported for recall.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: creative writing with an interactive AI
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered RCT in which participants write creatively with an interactive AI; those rewarded for originality relative to peers produce collectively more diverse writing than those rewarded for quality, mainly by copying fewer AI suggestions verbatim. The manipulation is the incentive, not AI access. Outside the core lane journals; reported for recall.
